job.title: Backend Engineer, Knowledge Graph (Rust)
job.pay_full: $115,200 – $162,000 a year base salary (United States range for this role's level; US residents)

details.about: GitLab is an intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps, with more than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100 using it. This intermediate-level role is on the GitLab Orbit team in the Data Engineering organization, which builds and runs the Knowledge Graph: a Rust backend that turns GitLab's software development lifecycle (SDLC) and code data into a property graph, using ClickHouse, NATS JetStream and the Data Insights Platform, and serves secure graph queries and MCP tools to GitLab Duo agents and product features. In the first year you'd own specific components or features, such as parts of the SDLC indexing pipeline or query paths.
duties: Build and improve features in the Rust-based Knowledge Graph service (query engine, SDLC and code indexing, API and MCP endpoints) with guidance from senior and staff engineers
Maintain integrations with the rest of GitLab: Rails, the Data Insights Platform (Siphon, NATS, ClickHouse) and the GitLab Duo Agent Platform
Contribute to system design discussions by proposing options, raising questions and documenting decisions
Improve operational maturity with metrics, logging, runbooks and alerts, and join the on-call rotation as appropriate for your level
Work asynchronously with product, data, infrastructure, security and AI counterparts to ship features safely
Use AI-assisted development workflows responsibly while keeping code quality high
Take part in code reviews, knowledge sharing and pairing
Pitch in across the stack when needed, including occasional Ruby work or small frontend changes
needs: Professional experience building and maintaining backend systems in production
Proficiency in at least one modern backend language and a strong interest in Rust: prior Rust experience or clear evidence you can ramp up quickly
Some exposure to distributed data or analytics systems (e.g. OLAP databases, Kafka- or NATS-style messaging, CDC pipelines), or strong motivation to learn them
Interest in graph data modeling and query patterns (property graphs, multi-step traversals, aggregations)
Practical experience with, or strong interest in, using AI tools in day-to-day development, with a thoughtful approach to checking their output
A language-agnostic mindset: able to pick up Ruby, Go or TypeScript/Vue as needed
Solid system design fundamentals for your level
Comfort in a low-process, high-ownership, all-remote team that communicates clearly in writing across time zones
details.benefits: US base salary range $115,200 – $162,000 a year for this role's level (for US residents; set through interviews and based on experience, skills and location; excludes bonuses, equity and benefits). GitLab supports full-time employees with benefits for health, finances and well-being, flexible paid time off, team member resource groups, equity compensation and an employee stock purchase plan, a growth and development fund, and parental leave.
notes: Remote role open in the United States and Canada; the salary range applies to US residents
GitLab welcomes candidates who don't meet every single requirement
Accommodations are available during the recruiting process
